summary: Re-review of cc8afbd..e9e7d36 (tasks 4.13i and 4.13j, the live Go quota answer) on top of my earlier audit edee50b..cc8afbd. F1 and F2 are fixed and verified live: `cd harness && npx tsx model-guide/quota.ts --provider opencode-go --base http://127.0.0.1:38307` prints {"provider":"opencode-go","source":"opencode-go","state":"ready","cap":3,"windows":{"5h":4.732990583333333,"weekly":1.8931962333333334,"monthly":0.9465981166666667}}. The Go branch reads the live key weekly (quota.ts:288-297), the null credits_balance window is skipped (quota.ts:274-281), the Go answer must hold both the 5h and the weekly name (quota.ts:319-325), and both runners key the Go rule on quota_provider (review-run.sh:257-265, judge-run.sh:237-249). F3 is fixed: probe-4.10.sh gates only opencode-go/* routes at 5h 95 or more / weekly 100 or more and reads windows["weekly"] (lines 60-76, 103-120). F4 is fixed: plan row 4.12 states the night limit 5h 95 % / week 100 % (plan.md:1873-1876). F5 is fixed: spec D14 says as test P2b pins (spec.md:721). Tests: review-run.test.ts 53 pass 0 fail; judge-run.test.ts 30 passed in the first run but J14 failed in 2 of 3 full runs on a global /proc scan that races the teardown of the earlier lock test under machine load, and J14 passes alone in 3.76 s; quota.test.ts gives 24 pass and 2 fail, and the 2 failures are the in-flight Red of task 4.13k (commits afef66e and 5085d9b, landed 02:01 +07 after the audited HEAD), not a defect of e9e7d36. But the 04:00 probe will not give the 3 pilot routes a correct line. I ran a transient user unit of my own, the same unit type as mg-probe-4-10.service, and it printed NO opencode, NO openchamber, and NO node: the systemd user PATH holds no nvm bin and no pnpm bin. At 04:00 +07 each route will record one refusal line, `<route> refused review-run: routes.json is unreadable exit=2`, because review-run.sh:230 runs `node -e` and node is not on the unit PATH; even with node the run would refuse at review-run.sh:277 (opencode resolves by `command -v`) and the Go quota read would stop at the port source (quota.ts:166 runs `openchamber status`). No reachable line means the nights of 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-22 skip every route with `skipped: <route> not reachable in probe-4.10`, no pass runs, and the first track A results of the phase cannot be produced by Sun 2026-11-22. The probe fires in under 2 hours.
blocking_findings: F8 (blocking, wiring, systemd transient unit environment of mg-probe-4-10.timer / mg-night-4-11-n1..n3.timer, proven with `systemd-run --user --wait --pipe --collect bash -c 'printf "PATH=%s" "$PATH"; command -v opencode || ...; command -v openchamber || ...; command -v node || ...'`): the transient unit PATH is /home/daniel-bo/.local/bin:/home/daniebo/.local/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/games:/usr/local/games:/snap/bin:/snap/bin, which holds no node (nvm bin /home/daniebo/.nvm/versions/node/v24.19.0/bin), no opencode, and no openchamber (/home/daniebo/.local/share/pnpm/bin). The probe driver itself works (git, curl, python3 are on the PATH, and its own curl gate reads the live 5h 4.73 / weekly 1.89 values), but heavy-run.sh sets no PATH, and review-run.sh refuses at line 230 (`node -e` for the routes.json row) with `review-run: routes.json is unreadable`, exit 2. So the 04:00 probe writes one refusal line per route instead of a probe line, probe-4.10.txt holds no `<route> reachable` line, and every night stops with `skipped: <route> not reachable in probe-4.10`. The existing lending-desk-daily.service proves the machine pattern: it sets `Environment=PATH=%h/.local/share/pnpm/bin:%h/.local/bin:%h/.nvm/versions/node/v24.19.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` for exactly this reason. Fix before 04:00 +07: add a PATH export to the top of probe-4.10.sh and night-4.11.sh (`export PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.19.0/bin:$HOME/.local/share/pnpm/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"`), and also export BENCH_QUOTA_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:38307 so review-run.sh never needs the openchamber port source; or re-create the four transient timers with a full PATH. A manual probe run from a login shell inside the 02:00-05:55 +07 window also works, because a login shell holds all three binaries.
nonblocking_findings: F6 kept and sharpened (minor, harness/model-guide-tests/judge-run.test.ts:1938 and :942-961): J14 asserts `liveFakeProcesses()` equals [] with no settle wait, and liveFakeProcesses scans every /proc entry for the text fake-opencode, so it sees any fake process on the whole machine, including the teardown of the earlier lock test that SIGKILLs its background holder (judge-run.test.ts:1553-1555). Tonight judge-run.test.ts gave 30 passed in one run and J14 failed in 2 of 3 full runs under a loaded machine (another session ran the review-run suite and other heavy jobs through the audit, load 4 to 6); the isolated run `npx vitest run ... -t 'J14 ends the call'` passes in 3.76 s with a clean pgrep, and each leftover died within seconds after the suite with its fixture dir deleted. The product contract holds; the assertion cannot prove it reliably under load. Fix: give J14 the same settle wait that J14b already uses at line 1975 (`waitFor(() => liveFakeProcesses().length === 0, 15_000)`), and scope the scan to the fixture pids where possible. The same fix covers the R12/afterAll flake of review-run.test.ts from my earlier F6.

F7 kept (nit, pre-existing, harness/model-guide/judge-run.sh:693-698): the 80 % stop branch stays dead for every sourced provider, because a window at 80 already gives the wait state and the wait branch at line 683 stops the run first; the comment at lines 670-673 still describes an 80 % stop that cannot occur. The 4.13i/4.13j diff did not touch this branch. Fix: drop the dead branch and fix the comment, or gate the wait branch at 80 for mid-run stops.
